title: Retire still-running legacy worker fleet
description: Home artifact audit found eight /bin/bash ./scripts/fleet-headless.sh N processes with cwd ~/Developer/lichen-workers/worker1 through worker8 (deleted), plus merge-janitor.sh and fleet-guards.sh 10. Existing workers are still issuing bd writes. User crontab runs */2 * * * * flock -n /tmp/fleet-watchdog.lock /home/mark/Developer/lichen-workspace/project-LICHEN/scripts/fleet-watchdog.sh; watchdog can recreate workers. Git worktree list only shows main. Obtain authorization to disable this exact watchdog entry and terminate identified legacy fleet processes; inspect current identities before signaling, preserve logs/work, do not stop unrelated tmux sessions or agents. worker2-build/cargo is ~1.67 GiB generated artifacts, cleanup candidate after fleet quiescence. No fleet shutdown or artifact deletion authorized/performed in audit.
acceptance_criteria: Authorized legacy fleet shutdown verified, watchdog cannot restart it, unrelated processes and saved recovery data preserved.
close_reason: User-authorized retirement: commented out exact two-minute watchdog crontab entry; verified cwd/argv/PGID and SIGTERM-stopped eight headless workers plus janitor and guard and all live members of their ten process groups. No force kill needed. After 125-second watchdog interval, corrected process check finds zero active fleet scripts and zero active watchdog cron entries. Idle tmux shell, logs, recovery artifacts and unrelated processes preserved.
